coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Sandler Neurosciences Center
record.summary: A ~237,000 sq ft, five-story neuroscience research building at 675 Nelson Rising Lane (OpenStreetMap) that houses about 100 principal investigators and more than 500 additional researchers and staff (Clark Construction), completed in 2012 (SOM; Clark Construction). The month of opening and the construction start are not sourced.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd in the repo's DataSF parcels copy) alone is about 12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: About 100 principal investigators and more than 500 additional researchers and staff

costs.what: Project cost stated on the developer's (Edgemoor) project page for the Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain partnership with UCSF; the page gives no date

milestones.text: Sandler Neurosciences Center completed (SOM's project page lists Completion Year 2012 and Clark Construction lists completion 2012; the month is not sourced -- a June 2012 Tradeline report cited earlier could not be read)

milestones.text: Sandler Neurosciences Center completed (SOM and Clark Construction list 2012; the month is not sourced)

changes.text: SOM's page gives 'Design Finish Year 2010' and 'Completion Year 2012' only, so the May 2010 construction start (a misreading of the design year) was removed and the opening is now the year 2012, also listed by Clark Construction. The $200 million cost and occupant counts had rested on a Tradeline article that could not be read; Clark Construction gives about 100 principal investigators and 500+ researchers and staff, and Edgemoor's project page gives a $208 million project cost. The unsourced 'SF office' detail was dropped and the aerial photo caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'.

open_questions: This record corrects this project's own earlier working assumption of a 2011 opening; May 2012 is well-supported by both the architect's own page and trade press.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, blocked to automated fetches with a 403); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further in this pass; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.

2026-09-29 accuracy audit: no readable source dates the start of construction (SOM gives only 'Design Finish Year 2010'; the earlier '2010-05 construction begins' had no source) or the opening month (SOM and Clark give the year 2012 only); the Tradeline June 2012 article that gave May 2012, $200 million and the occupant counts returned 403 and could not be read. The project cost is now the $208 million on Edgemoor's project page (undated), which conflicts with the $200 million earlier attributed to Tradeline.

record.notes: ~237,000 sq ft, five stories (SOM; Clark Construction); houses about 100 principal investigators and more than 500 additional researchers and staff (Clark Construction); project cost $208 million per the developer's (Edgemoor) project page.
